drafts.fullDescription:
Sahara — A Palliative Care Companion

Keep goals-of-care conversations, daily care and useful information together for patients, families and care teams.

Keep the words that matter
Record a conversation with everyone's permission, dictate a speaker's turn on a supported phone, or type it. Review the original words, keep earlier note versions and share the exact version you discussed. In shared care, clinical review requires independent clinician approval and a separate patient invitation. Patient and family confirmations are recorded separately.

Follow daily care
Keep prescribed medicines, appointments, questions and tasks together. Keep baseline symptom details for quicker follow-ups, with fresh 0–10 or unrated answers, observation times and separate sadness and worry ratings. View dated severity trends for matching context. Rotate the 3D body and tap a pain location, or use the body-area buttons. Saved points follow your care record; red intensity follows your entered pain rating. This is a personal diary, not ESAS-r/IPOS, a diagnosis or a clinical risk score. Optional reminders can be delayed by phone settings and are not an emergency service.

Find palliative care centres
Browse 1,631 published listings across 36 Indian states and union territories. Search the list, open a map, call a centre or get directions. Listings include dated sources and do not confirm current services or medicine stock. Call before travelling.

Keep and read your reports
Add PDFs or photos to Documents. Read printed English and Hindi text on your phone, compare it with the original and correct it before saving medicine details or copied facts. The Documents flow keeps original files on the phone unless you choose to share a copy. Its local OCR does not upload them.

Optional Hindi and English tools
Transcribe a saved, consented recording locally with Qwen3-ASR after a separate 987 MB model download. This requires a supported 64-bit phone and sufficient free memory. There is no cloud speech fallback. Check names, numbers and mixed-language words against the recording before using the text.
Optional Hindi–English translation runs on your phone after a language-pack download. The original remains available. Machine translation is not a clinical interpretation.

Doctor test workspace
Explore separate fictional test patients with your Sahara login. Save test drafts, note versions and reported doses to your account. Separately chosen, permitted test recordings, PDFs or report images can be uploaded to private Supabase storage. Uploading does not transcribe or analyse them and grants no clinical access. Use no real patient or confidential files. Request removal of online test files through support; uninstalling does not delete them.

Choose what you share
Basic records work without an account. Sign in to save care records and share permitted information with people you invite. Symptom notes saved in that account follow its sharing rules. Unsent phone drafts, recordings and original report files are not automatically uploaded. Text you explicitly save or send to shared care is stored with your account. There are no ads. Google ML Kit sends technical usage metrics and diagnostics as explained in the privacy policy.

Sahara is not a medical device. It does not diagnose, treat, cure or prevent a medical condition, recommend treatment or replace professional medical care. Ask a qualified healthcare professional for medical advice. Care notes record a discussion; they are not prescriptions or legal directives.
drafts.releaseNotes: Add dated symptom trends, separate sadness and worry ratings, quicker follow-ups and a rotatable 3D pain-location map. The connected doctor test workspace saves fictional notes and reported doses, with separate permission for selected private file uploads. Hindi/English local reading tools and the national care-centre directory remain available.

Doctor workspace > Patients has separate account-backed test records; selected file uploads require permission and no patient data. This grants no clinician approval. Real clinical review needs existing independent approval and a patient invitation. Local ASR requires a 987 MB download and supported phone.

Symptom diary stores fresh ratings/unrated answers, dates, pain regions/points and matching-context trends. It does not administer ESAS-r/IPOS, diagnose, or decide treatment.
Doctor account workspace has a separate fictional dataset. Drafts/test versions and reported doses persist online; sample schedules do not dispatch invitations or reserve appointments.

Selected test recordings/audio/PDF/images up to 4 MiB have separate explicit permission and Upload actions to private Supabase storage. Uploading does not perform AI/OCR/transcription. No real patient/confidential files.
Local Qwen ASR needs a 987,015,347-byte download, 64-bit process and 2.5 GiB available memory. Local OCR/translation inputs stay local; explicit test-storage uploads are separate.
Real shared review requires existing independent clinician approval and separate patient invitation. Check actual restricted reviewer access; fabricate no verification or authority.

No individual doctor-test file deletion control exists. Verified-email requests need separate protected-object and test-row support handling. No live purge or full signed-in upload service test established by this source audit.
